narr: A low pressure system moved northward from the Central Plains to the Northern Plains on May 12th and lifted a warm front across the Northland bringing two rounds of storms to the region. The first round during the afternoon hours were prolific hail producing storms with the largest hail stones being ping pong ball sized. Another round of storms arrived during the early evening hours and contained strong winds that moved through the Brainerd Lakes area. A maximum gust of 61 mph was recorded at the Brainerd Airport leading to widespread tree damage in the area. As storms continued overnight, heavy rainfall along the North Shore led to Flash Flooding in Lake and Cook counties with numerous road washouts reported.
ev: A washout was reported along Breezy Lane in Finland.
Multiple washouts were reported along Cramer Road near and east of Finland.

A photo was received showing Moose Valley Road flooded at Carlson Creek with water flowing over the road surface. A later report indicated the Cook County Highway Department closed the road at 6:30 AM CDT.

A local TV meteorologist forwarded photos from a viewer showing a culvert that had washed out on Hill Road near Floodwood. There was a roughly 6 foot gap in the road that was at least 3 to 4 feet deep where the flow of the creek exceeded the capacity of the culvert and washed out the road. The viewers that sent the photos were unable to leave their property by vehicle and had to make a makeshift footbridge to get to town.
